newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Dollar licks wounds after mark bites back.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Dollar licks wounds after mark bites back.

text.p: The dollar stumbled toward support levels on both sides of 1.71 marks Friday, just three days after posting a three-year high at 1.7375.
Technical analysts cited weakness in dollar/Swiss and surging mark/yen and mark/lira crosses for dollar/mark's sudden heaviness.
"Dollar/Swiss had been a ball-and-chain all week on dollar/mark and mark/yen exaggerated the dollar's move down," said Keith Raphael, president of Crosscurrents Investment Advisory.
Mark/yen's rally to 73.50 coincided with the dollar's decline through supports at 1.7230 and 1.7170 marks on the way to a tentative resting point near 171.20 on Friday.
The mark appears to have emerged in good condition after a brief bout of profit-taking and should resume its climb in coming sessions, chartists said.
"Mark/yen came down to a corrective objective at 72.60 and held very well. We saw some short-covering above 73.05," Raphael said.
Meanwhile, dollar/mark could face more selling pressure to the 1.7085/95 area, a Fibonacci retracement level.
Foreign Exchange Analytics partner David Solin noted that that level corresponds to a 38.2-percent retracement of the rally from the March 31 low at 1.6610 to the Tuesday high at 1.7375.
"I wouldn't be surprised to see dollar/mark a little bit below (1.71) the figure. I suspect there may be a little bit of support there," said Solin.

Dollar/yen has spent the last two days quietly orbiting 126, hemmed in by persistent talk of central bank intervention to slow the dollar's climb despite the implied dollar/yen boost in the mark/yen rally.
"Dollar/yen has basically been stuck against a 126.26 medium-term resistance level," Raphael said.
Should the market shake off the intervention fears, the greenback should continue its assault on multi-year highs, revisiting the 127 range in coming sessions, chartists said.
